lexicon.title: Từ điển đọc
lexicon.subtitle: Readings apply to the voice step's reading text only; display text, titles and captions keep the correct term
lexicon.intro: The dictionary applies to the reading text at voice synthesis only: terms in the reading script are replaced by their defined readings so the voice reads them right. Display subtitles keep the original terms. Locked entries cannot be edited or toggled by bulk operations until unlocked. Enabling an entry still marked “Not ASR-verified” always needs its own confirmation. The ASR check button only queues verification, it never enables an entry; verdicts are recorded back onto each entry.
lexicon.showing: Showing {{shown}}/{{total}} entries matching the current filters.
lexicon.confirmEnableUnverified: {{count}} entries have not passed ASR verification. Enabling them is the channel owner's call — continue?
lexicon.confirmEnableOne: This entry has not passed ASR verification. Enabling it is the channel owner's call — continue?
lexicon.emptyFiltered: No entries match the current filters.
lexicon.importTitle: Import the dictionary from a file (JSON / CSV / TXT)
lexicon.importHint: Import: JSON (the wrapped {format: "diemtin-lexicon", version: 1, entries: [...]}, an array of {term, reading, scope, category_scope, note, enabled}, or a {term: reading} map), CSV (term,reading columns or the form's Vietnamese headers), TXT (one entry per line, split by =>, tab or :). Every file is format-checked (term ≤ 120 chars, reading ≤ 200, scope/category_scope must be standard codes, enabled must be boolean) and previewed before anything is written; a file broken at the format level is rejected whole. Exports use the same schema, so they re-import verbatim.

voice.title: Voice
voice.priorityHint: One priority list for every engine: drag the handle (or use the up/down arrow buttons) to reorder; the voice step walks from the highest priority down when an engine fails. The voice Relay is a separate route (tts.danhthanh.dev) — its card stays in the same list to preserve the fallback order and is marked separately, so it is never confused with the self-hosted or API engines. A disabled engine leaves the chain but keeps its voice configuration; enable it again and add it back when needed. Changes take effect only after you press Save voice configuration.
voice.enableToAdd: Enable the engine to add it to the chain
voice.subtitle: The channel's voice engines: packages installed on this machine or models called over API; the fallback chain is the order tried when an engine fails
voice.chainHint: The voice step tries the engines in this order for every beat; a failed engine falls through to the next. An engine in the chain must be enabled.
voice.addEngine: Add an enabled engine to the chain

journal.title: Journal
journal.subtitle: Operation log of the video module: lexicon, voice configuration, video actions
journal.heading: Not implemented yet — awaiting the logging module
journal.body: The operation-log recording module for actions inside the PipelineX app (lexicon, voice, videos) has not been built yet, so this page has no real data and shows no fabricated list. Engine-level actions and the YouTube operations are already recorded in the system's central Audit Log. The specification package for the logging module lives in specs/001-operation-log in this repo; when the module is approved and implemented, the real journal page will take this exact place.
